newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: BP Chemicals pressing ahead with China projects.
newsitem.headline: BP Chemicals pressing ahead with China projects.

text.p: BP Chemicals, a unit of British Petroleum, is pressing ahead with its investments in Asia, including in China, helping to allay fears that investment policies might suffer following the death of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping.

"I don't see any change after Deng. It is not as if the news was a shock," BP Chemicals chief executive officer, Bryan Sanderson, told reporters on the sidelines of the second Asia Pacific Chemical Conference in Singapore.
Sanderson said BP was hoping to start up the first plant at its U.S.$2.5 billion joint-venture with Shanghai Petrochemicals Co Ltd in 1999 in Jinshan, near Shanghai.
BP also started construction of a U.S.$200 million acetic acid plant in the south west Chinese province of Sichuan. The 150,000 tonne-per-year plant is due to start up in 1998.

Energy analysts have said they did not see any changes to China's energy investment policies following the death of the reform-minded Deng. However, they said decisions on projects could be delayed while the power vacuum is filled, they said.
As reported earlier, BP said on Tuesday it plans to build a 500,000-tonne-per-year U.S.$200 million acetic acid plant in Malaysia.

In Indonesia, BP has joined a consortium of four Japanese firms and one Indonesian firm to work on a feasibility study for the building a 700,000-tonnes-per-year ethylene plant, which is expected to go on stream in 2000.
